Prepare Multi-State Data from an OMOP Cohort Table

Source: R/prepareMultistateData.R
prepareMultiStateData.Rd

Convert cohort-defined state entries into counting-process data for multi-state survival models using the survival and mstate packages.

Usage

prepareMultistateData(
  cohort,
  trans,
  eventDate = "cohort_start_date",
  censorDate = NULL,
  stateHierarchy = character(),
  stateStep = 0.01
)

Arguments

cohort

A cohort_table object containing one cohort for each state in the multi-state model. Cohort names must match the state names in trans.

trans

Transition matrix describing the states and transitions in the multi-state model. If S is the number of states in the multi-state model, trans should be an S x S matrix, with (i,j)-element a positive integer if a transition from i to j is possible in the multi-state model, NA otherwise. In particular, all diagonal elements should be NA. The integers indicating the possible transitions in the multi-state model should be sequentially numbered, 1,...,K, with K the number of transitions. Row and column names must be identical, unique state names in the same order. A row containing only NA defines an absorbing state. Use transMat() to build a matrix.

eventDate

Name of the date column in cohort that identifies when an individual enters a state. State entries are defined by these dates; reaching cohort_end_date does not automatically create a state change.

censorDate

Name of the date column in cohort that identifies the end of follow-up, inclusive. If NULL, the end of each individual's observation period is used. Missing values in a supplied column also fall back to the observation period end. Supplied dates replace the observation-based dates; they are not automatically capped at observation end. Use the same date on all state records for a person when specifying a single follow-up endpoint. Individuals with no follow-up after their index date are excluded from the analysis.

stateHierarchy

Character vector of state names in the order used to resolve states that occur on the same date, with earlier entries occurring first. An empty character vector applies no hierarchy; unresolved ties between competing states cause an error. Include all states that need a distinct order. Unlisted states share the priority of the last listed state.

stateStep

Numeric increment used to separate states that occur on the same date according to stateHierarchy, in days. Successive priority ranks are shifted by multiples of this increment. The default is 0.01 days.

Value

An msdata data frame with one row per possible outgoing transition for each interval at risk. Columns include subject_id, integer state identifiers from and to, transition identifier trans, elapsed days Tstart and Tstop, and status (1 for the observed transition, 0 otherwise). from_name and to_name contain the state names. The transition matrix is retained in the trans attribute.

Details

Time zero is each person's earliest entry into a state with at least one outgoing transition. People recorded only in absorbing states cannot enter the analysis. At each step, the earliest subsequent entry permitted by trans determines the next state. Repeated visits are supported when the matrix permits returning to a previous state. Cohort end dates alone do not create exits; provide a cohort for each destination state.

Events on the censor date are included. After records beyond their censor dates are removed, the latest remaining censor date for each person is used for their trajectory. People with no follow-up after time zero are excluded before applying stateHierarchy. If the hierarchy shifts a same-day event beyond the censor date, follow-up is extended to include the shifted event.

Informational messages report excluded records: events after censoring, people without an eligible initial state, events before time zero, people with no follow-up after time zero, and states that cannot be reached under trans. Counts refer to records, rather than distinct people. Remaining simultaneous competing states cause an error; use stateHierarchy to order them.

State records are collected into R for processing, including when cohort is stored in a database.

See also

summariseMultistateProbabilities(), transMat()

Examples

library(CohortConstructor)
library(dplyr)
library(omock)
library(OmopMultistate)

cdm <- mockCdmFromDataset(datasetName = "GiBleed")
#> ℹ Loading bundled GiBleed tables from package data.
#> ℹ Adding drug_strength table.
#> ℹ Creating local <cdm_reference> object.

# An illustrative concept set: aspirin 81 mg oral tablets.
# Keep the first treatment episode for each person.
cdm$treated <- conceptCohort(
  cdm = cdm,
  conceptSet = list(treated = 19059056L),
  name = "treated"
) |>
  requireIsFirstEntry()
#> ℹ Subsetting table drug_exposure using 1 concept with domain: drug.
#> ℹ Combining tables.
#> ℹ Creating cohort attributes.
#> ℹ Applying cohort requirements.
#> ℹ Merging overlapping records.
#> ✔ Cohort treated created.

# Enter the untreated state the day after treatment ends. Require that day
# to be within observation, so loss to follow-up is not a discontinuation.
cdm$untreated <- cdm$treated |>
  padCohortEnd(days = 1L, requireFullContribution = TRUE, name = "untreated") |>
  padCohortDate(
    days = 0L,
    indexDate = "cohort_end_date",
    cohortDate = "cohort_start_date"
  ) |>
  renameCohort("untreated")
cdm <- bind(cdm$treated, cdm$untreated, name = "states")

# Model first discontinuation: untreated is an absorbing state.
# Matrix state names must match the cohort names.
trans <- transMat(
  x = list(2, integer()),
  names = c("treated", "untreated")
)

# By default, follow-up ends at the end of each person's observation period.
# Resolve any same-day states by placing treatment before discontinuation.
msData <- prepareMultistateData(
  cohort = cdm$states,
  trans = trans,
  stateHierarchy = c("treated", "untreated")
)

# One row per possible transition and time interval; status = 1 is an event.
msData |>
  arrange(subject_id, Tstart) |>
  head()
#> An object of class 'msdata'
#> 
#> Data:
#>   subject_id from to trans Tstart Tstop status from_name   to_name
#> 1          1    1  2     1      0    29      1   treated untreated
#> 2          2    1  2     1      0    15      1   treated untreated
#> 3          3    1  2     1      0    22      1   treated untreated
#> 4          5    1  2     1      0    68      1   treated untreated
#> 5          6    1  2     1      0    15      1   treated untreated
#> 6          7    1  2     1      0    15      1   treated untreated

cdmDisconnect(cdm)
